title: Binary grafting and canary validation for GPU dependency upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description: We need a low-risk upgrade path for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS library updates that minimizes blast radius for production fleets. This ticket implements a binary-level grafting technique: produce small binary delta artifacts that patch runtime symbol resolution and entry points at startup, together with an automated canary validation harness that runs micro-benchmarks, smoke-model passes, and KV-cache integrity checks across representative GPU variants. The goal is to enable rolling updates of GPU dependency bundles with quick automatic rollback if regressions are detected. This differs from full shims or rebuilding all bundles; grafting aims to be compact, reversible, and testable within the existing deploy pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Produce binary graft artifacts for at least one CUDA+Triton+CUTLASS upgrade (example: CUDA 12.3 -> 13.0 candidate).
Canary harness runs end-to-end in CI and verifies correctness on at least three GPU types (A100, H100, T4) within 30 minutes total wall time.
End-to-end canary metrics captured: token/sec regression <= 1.5% and 95th p99 latency regression <= 5ms for reference workloads; any larger regression triggers automatic rollback.
Rollback protocol exercised in staging and documented runbook added to runbooks/confluence/gpu-binary-grafting.md.
A follow-up PR merges the graft generation and validation steps into the runtime release pipeline without increasing median startup latency by >2ms.
Security review checklist complete for binary patch signing and verification.
technical_notes: Binary grafting approach: generate ELF/so deltas that replace or intercept only the changed symbol table entries and small function trampolines; avoid wholesale library replacements.
Use deterministic build artifacts and content-based signatures; grafts include a metadata header with compatible symbol list and ABI fingerprint.
Runtime loader change: add a gated graft-apply stage that performs verification (signature + checksum) and exposes dry-run flag to skip apply for baseline validation.

Canary harness: existing perf fixtures (in runtime/test/perf) adapted to run in parallel across GPU types using resource-isolated k8s jobs; harness produces JSON metrics to be compared against golden baselines.

Fallback/rollback mechanism: if graft fails verification or canary metrics fall outside thresholds, mark node unschedulable and trigger artifact rollback via orchestration agent (k8s DaemonSet rolling restart flows).
Trade-offs: grafting keeps artifact size small and allows quicker rollout, but increases complexity in loader and debuggability — include verbose logging and symbol map dump option.
Compatibility heuristics: include ABI fingerprint heuristics and symbol-level compatibility checks; for non-compatible signatures, fail fast and route to full-bundle upgrade path.
Testing: add synthetic fuzz of symbol resolution to detect edge-cases where inlined functions or LTO change offsets.
rollout_plan: 1) Generate graft for candidate CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS bundle in feature branch.
2) Run CI graft verification (unit tests + loader dry-run) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
3) Canary stage: deploy graft to isolated staging pool (small set of nodes across GPU types) and run full canary harness.
4) Monitor metrics for 2 hours; if stable, expand to 30% of fleet with controlled quiescent periods between waves.
5) If regression detected at any wave, auto-trigger rollback and create postmortem ticket referencing this issue.
6) After successful rollout, publish graft artifact to signed-artifacts registry and tag runtime release with graft metadata.
7) Document observed regressions and improvements in release notes and telemetry dashboards.
testing_plan: Unit tests for graft generator: symbol selection, delta packing, signature verification.
Integration tests: loader apply/dry-run on minimal runtime image across CPU-only and GPU CI runners.
Performance canary: token/sec and latency benchmarks against Golden for small, medium, and long sequences.
Stress tests: run continuous decode loops for 6 hours on representative model to surface memory corruption or KV-cache mismatches.
Compatibility tests: run model correctness checks (logprobs, top-k outputs) on a fixed prompt set and compare to baseline tolerances.
Chaos step: simulate partial graft application failures and ensure rollback is safe.
risks: Binary graft might miss edge-case symbol usages introduced by aggressive compiler optimizations, causing subtle corruption.
Increased loader complexity could make debugging GPU crashes harder; requires strong logging and symbol maps.
Canary coverage may not catch long-tail regressions that only appear under production traffic patterns.
Signing/key-management errors could prevent grafts from being applied; rotation procedures must be validated.
Rollout timing constraints: graft verification in CI must finish within existing release windows or release cadence will be impacted.
